problem.name: Set disjointness in two-party communication
problem.statement_latex: Alice and Bob hold $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$ and decide whether $\sum_i x_iy_i=0$, with error at most $1/3$. Complexity counts two-way communication; local computation is free.
problem.statement_text: Alice and Bob hold $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$ and decide whether $\sum_i x_iy_i=0$, with error at most $1/3$. Complexity counts two-way communication; local computation is free.

strength.description_latex: A tight quadratic communication improvement arising from quantum search.
strength.description_text: A tight quadratic communication improvement arising from quantum search.

evidence.description_latex: Both classical and quantum bounded-error communication complexities have matching lower bounds.
evidence.description_text: Both classical and quantum bounded-error communication complexities have matching lower bounds.

hardware.description_latex: Coherent quantum links and distributed search registers; total communication is $\Theta(\sqrt n)$ qubits.
hardware.description_text: Coherent quantum links and distributed search registers; total communication is $\Theta(\sqrt n)$ qubits.

quantum.headline_latex: $\Theta(\sqrt n)$ communicated qubits. Aaronson--Ambainis distributed search finds an index with $x_i=y_i=1$ and removes the logarithmic overhead of straightforward index-register communication.
quantum.headline_text: $\Theta(\sqrt n)$ communicated qubits. Aaronson–Ambainis distributed search finds an index with $x_i=y_i=1$ and removes the logarithmic overhead of straightforward index-register communication.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(n)$ randomized classical bits, achieved by sending one input and matched by lower bounds. The quantum $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ lower bound also holds with prior entanglement.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(n)$ randomized classical bits, achieved by sending one input and matched by lower bounds. The quantum $\Omega(\sqrt n)$ lower bound also holds with prior entanglement.
